title: Copilot Studio Ask with Adaptive Card: contact details form with variable mapping
summary: A form card for the Ask with Adaptive Card node: required name and email, topic list and urgent toggle, with the output variable names and branching logic for Submit versus Cancel.
body:
In Copilot Studio the Ask with Adaptive Card node shows a card, waits for the user to press a button, and puts each input into an output variable named after the input id. That replaces a chain of five question nodes with one friendly card.

## Card JSON

```json
{
  "type": "AdaptiveCard",
  "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json",
  "version": "1.5",
  "body": [
    {
      "type": "TextBlock",
      "text": "Tell us how to reach you",
      "wrap": true,
      "size": "Medium",
      "weight": "Bolder"
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Text",
      "id": "fullName",
      "label": "Full name",
      "isRequired": true,
      "errorMessage": "Name is required",
      "maxLength": 80
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Text",
      "id": "email",
      "label": "Email",
      "style": "email",
      "isRequired": true,
      "errorMessage": "Enter an email address"
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.ChoiceSet",
      "id": "topic",
      "label": "What do you need help with?",
      "style": "compact",
      "value": "billing",
      "choices": [
        {
          "title": "Billing question",
          "value": "billing"
        },
        {
          "title": "Technical problem",
          "value": "tech"
        },
        {
          "title": "Something else",
          "value": "other"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Toggle",
      "id": "urgent",
      "title": "This is urgent",
      "valueOn": "true",
      "valueOff": "false",
      "value": "false"
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "Action.Submit",
      "title": "Continue",
      "data": {
        "action": "submit"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "Action.Submit",
      "title": "Cancel",
      "associatedInputs": "none",
      "data": {
        "action": "cancel"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## How to use

1. In a topic add a node: Ask a question > Ask with Adaptive Card. Open the node properties, choose Edit adaptive card and paste the JSON.
2. Under Output, map the variables. Every input id becomes an output you can use later: fullName, email, topic, urgent, plus the data property action from the pressed button.
3. Add a Condition after the node: if Topic.action is cancel, send a short message and end the topic; otherwise continue.
4. Use the values: in a message write "Thanks, {Topic.fullName}. We will write to {Topic.email}." and for urgent route by a condition on Topic.urgent being "true" (the toggle returns text).
5. If the user never submits and sends another message, the node can time out or re-prompt; configure the "no response" behavior in the node and keep a Cancel button.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the toggle value as boolean. valueOn and valueOff are text in the card; compare with the string "true".
- Forgetting associatedInputs none on Cancel. Without it a user with an empty required field cannot cancel.
- Using the card for sensitive data such as passwords or payment numbers. The values land in conversation variables and the transcript; do not collect them in a chat card.
- Mapping the variable type manually to Number for a text input. Keep text variables and convert with Value() in a Power Fx formula.
- Copying a card designed for Teams that uses Action.Execute. The Ask with Adaptive Card node works with Action.Submit.

## Compatibility notes

- Copilot Studio renders cards in the test chat, Teams and the web chat; rendering of newer elements such as Table varies by channel, so test in each channel you publish to.
- Version 1.5 is a safe maximum for Teams; if a channel shows the card without styling, reduce to 1.3, which this form also satisfies (label, isRequired and errorMessage need 1.3).
- Card text can also be formula-driven in the node; JSON stays the portable definition.
- Keep the card free of images from external domains unless you control them; use contoso.example or your own CDN in real projects.

title: Onboarding checklist card with an at-mention entity and full-width layout
summary: A welcome card that mentions a user via msteams entities, shows a checklist of toggles and saves progress with Action.Submit, with the rules for mention ids in bots and Workflows.
body:
Mentions make a card notify the person it is about. In Adaptive Cards for Teams this takes two parts: an <at>Name</at> tag inside a TextBlock and a matching entry in msteams.entities at the card root. This card welcomes a new hire and tracks a first-week checklist.

## Card JSON

```json
{
  "type": "AdaptiveCard",
  "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json",
  "version": "1.5",
  "msteams": {
    "width": "Full",
    "entities": [
      {
        "type": "mention",
        "text": "<at>Alex Contoso</at>",
        "mentioned": {
          "id": "alex@contoso.example",
          "name": "Alex Contoso"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "body": [
    {
      "type": "TextBlock",
      "text": "Welcome to the team, <at>Alex Contoso</at>",
      "wrap": true,
      "size": "Large",
      "weight": "Bolder"
    },
    {
      "type": "TextBlock",
      "text": "Here is your first-week checklist. Tick items as you finish them.",
      "wrap": true
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Toggle",
      "id": "laptop",
      "title": "Pick up laptop and badge",
      "valueOn": "done",
      "valueOff": "open",
      "value": "open"
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Toggle",
      "id": "mfa",
      "title": "Set up multi-factor sign-in",
      "valueOn": "done",
      "valueOff": "open",
      "value": "open"
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Toggle",
      "id": "teams",
      "title": "Join the team channels",
      "valueOn": "done",
      "valueOff": "open",
      "value": "open"
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Toggle",
      "id": "intro",
      "title": "Introduce yourself in the General channel",
      "valueOn": "done",
      "valueOff": "open",
      "value": "open"
    },
    {
      "type": "Input.Text",
      "id": "question",
      "label": "Anything blocking you?",
      "isMultiline": true,
      "placeholder": "Optional"
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "Action.Submit",
      "title": "Save progress",
      "data": {
        "intent": "onboardingProgress",
        "user": "alex@contoso.example"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "Action.OpenUrl",
      "title": "Open onboarding hub",
      "url": "https://contoso.example/onboarding"
    }
  ]
}
```

## How to use

1. Replace the mention text and ids. The text of the entity must be exactly the same as the tag in the TextBlock, including the name inside <at></at>.
2. In a bot, use the Teams user id (29:...) or the Microsoft Entra object id from the conversation members. In Workflows (the Teams "Post card" actions) and incoming webhooks, the id is the user's email address (UPN).
3. Store the checklist: on Save progress read laptop, mfa, teams, intro and question from the posted data and write them to a Microsoft List or Dataverse row keyed by the user value.
4. When the person has finished, replace the card with a "done" version or post a short congratulation, so the checklist does not stay open for months.
5. To mention several people add one entity per person and one tag per person; ids must be unique per entity.

## Common mistakes

- A mismatch between <at> text and entity text. The mention is then shown as plain text without a notification.
- Putting the entities array into body or at the wrong level. It belongs inside the msteams object at the card root.
- Using display names as ids. Mentions need a resolvable id, otherwise Teams ignores them.
- Mentioning someone in a card sent through a channel that the person cannot see. They are notified, but the card is not visible to them.
- Using valueOn and valueOff with booleans. They are strings; compare with "done" in your handler.

## Compatibility notes

- The msteams property (width, entities) is a Teams extension; other hosts ignore it. Mentions in Adaptive Cards need a card in a Teams message and are not supported in Outlook.
- Input.Toggle, Input.Text with isMultiline and label are supported by Teams in all current clients; label needs schema 1.3.
- Do not put real email addresses in sample cards; the example uses the reserved domain contoso.example.
- If you need more than about ten checklist items, move the list into a task app or a Planner board and keep the card to a summary with Action.OpenUrl.
